title: Hinokitiol ameliorates MASH in mice by therapeutic targeting of hepatic Nrf2 and inhibiting hepatocyte ferroptosis.
authors: Yin, Xunzhe; Liu, Zuojia; Li, Chang; Wang, Jin
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究天然化合物Hinokitiol通过Nrf2/GPX4信号抑制肝细胞铁死亡以改善代谢相关脂肪性肝炎，属于疾病机制与药理学研究，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或AI/物理模拟方法。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), an advanced stage of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), still lacks approved effective clinical drugs. Ferroptosis, a form of regulated cell death driven by excessive iron accumulation and uncontrollable lipid peroxidation, has been proven to be a trigger of inflammation and initiation of steatohepatitis. The pathogenic interplay is modulated by oxidative stress, while the Nrf2-mediated antioxidant response plays a regulatory role in ferroptosis. Phytochemical hinokitiol (Hino) has demonstrated positive efficacy in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) in the reported work, but it remains unknown whether its therapeutic effect attributes to delaying the progress of steatohepatitis to HCC. PURPOSE: This work aimed to systemically investigate the significance of ferroptosis in the pathogenesis of MASH and to demonstrate that Hino, a bioactive monoterpene compound, attenuates the primary pathological characteristics of MASH via promotion of Nrf2/GPX4 signaling. METHODS: In this work, a MASH model was established using the high-fat/high-cholesterol (HFHC) diet-fed in vivo and palmitic acid/oleic acid (PO)-stimulated hepatocytes in vitro. Biochemical indexes, pathological analysis, western blot, PCR assay, energy metabolic phenotype, molecular docking, and confirmatory assays were performed comprehensively to reveal the key link between the Nrf2/GPX4 axis and the treatment of MASH. RESULTS: Under MASH conditions with increased oxidative stress, we show that Nrf2 was remarkable downregulated in HFHC diet-fed mice and PO-managed hepatocytes. Mechanistically, hepatic upregulation of Nrf2 through phytochemical Hino supplementation inhibited ferroptosis, enhanced lipid metabolism, and thereby alleviated hepatic steatosis, inflammation, and fibrosis. Conversely, silencing Nrf2 in hepatocytes further promoted the accumulation of key markers of ferroptosis and aggravated MASH phenotypes. CONCLUSION: Increased ferroptosis promoted steatosis which further drove inflammation and hepatic fibrosis. Our results suggested the significance of Nrf2 in ameliorating MASH, which was regulated through Hino. Thus, targeted inhibition of ferroptosis through Hino administration is a feasible and effective approach for treating MASH.
abstract_zh: 背景：代谢功能障碍相关脂肪性肝炎（MASH）是代谢功能障碍相关脂肪性肝病（MASLD）的晚期阶段，目前仍缺乏获批的有效临床药物。铁死亡（ferroptosis）是一种由过量铁积累和不可控脂质过氧化驱动的调节性细胞死亡形式，已被证明是炎症的触发因素及脂肪性肝炎的起始因素。其致病性相互作用受氧化应激调节，而Nrf2介导的抗氧化反应在铁死亡中发挥调控作用。植物化学物质桧木醇（hinokitiol, Hino）在已报道的研究中对肝细胞癌（HCC）显示出积极疗效，但其治疗作用是否归因于延缓脂肪性肝炎向HCC的进展仍不清楚。目的：本研究旨在系统探讨铁死亡在MASH发病机制中的重要性，并证明Hino（一种生物活性单萜化合物）通过促进Nrf2/GPX4信号通路减轻MASH的主要病理特征。方法：本研究采用高脂/高胆固醇（HFHC）饮食喂养建立体内MASH模型，以及棕榈酸/油酸（PO）刺激的体外肝细胞模型。综合运用生化指标检测、病理分析、蛋白质印迹、PCR检测、能量代谢表型分析、分子对接及验证实验，揭示Nrf2/GPX4轴与MASH治疗之间的关键联系。结果：在氧化应激增加的MASH条件下，我们发现HFHC饮食喂养小鼠和PO处理的肝细胞中Nrf2显著下调。机制上，通过植物化学物质Hino补充实现肝脏Nrf2上调，抑制了铁死亡，增强了脂质代谢，从而减轻了肝脏脂肪变性、炎症和纤维化。相反，在肝细胞中沉默Nrf2进一步促进了铁死亡关键标志物的积累，并加重了MASH表型。结论：铁死亡增加促进了脂肪变性，进而驱动炎症和肝纤维化。我们的结果表明Nrf2在改善MASH中的重要性，且该过程受Hino调控。因此，通过Hino给药靶向抑制铁死亡是治疗MASH的一种可行且有效的方法。
